newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says won't give up on tax reform plan.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says won't give up on tax reform plan.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Tuesday he would do everything possible to realise government tax reforms even though they had been blocked by the opposition Social Democrats (SPD).
Waigel accused the SPD of pursuing a "confrontation course" in parliament's mediation process and said he would follow his tax reform drive up to next year's general election if necessary.

"It has become clear that the SPD is on a confrontation course, and that above all it is living up to its name as a party of tax increases," Waigel told reporters shortly before the coalition and SPD ended two days of informal talks on tax without reaching any agreement.

The two sides meet again on Wednesday in a formal session of parliament's mediation committee, but saw no chance of a deal on Waigel's plan to slash taxes which had earlier been rejected by the SPD-controlled Bundesrat upper house.
Waigel added: "The SPD is not in the slightest bit interested in a serious tax reform."

He saw some chances of a deal to end a row which has run for over two years to abolish a capital trading tax on companies. But he rejected SPD proposals on financing a cut in occupational insurance charges to trim labour costs and help fight high German unemployment.

Rejection by the mediation committee will send the tax reforms back to the lower house of parliament, which meets next Tuesday. Coalition negotiators said they were considering invoking parliamentary mediation again.
Although that is unlikely to change the SPD's opposition to government tax policies, Waigel said he would carry on fighting for his reform project.

"We will do all that is humanly possible...to defend our tax reform," he said. "Even if the SPD rejects the tax reform in the mediation committee or in the Bundesrat it will stay on the agenda -- this year, next year and after the parliamentary elections."
